findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext drops everything logged through it
findings.body: `FromContext` returns a brand-new `TestLogger`. `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now logs only through `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)` (logger_middleware.go:58). So if a test injects a `TestLogger`, its `InfoLogs` will never record the "Plugin Request Completed" call, and that log line can't be asserted. Returning `f` (or a logger that shares its `Logs` state) would keep the fake usable for this middleware.

findings.title: No tests for the new middleware or the fields the logger middleware now gets from context
findings.body: The `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID`, `uname` and `traceID` fields used to be added explicitly in `logRequest`. Now they only show up if `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` sits before `LoggerMiddleware` in `CreateMiddlewares` and the infra logger's context providers fill them in. There's no `contextual_logger_middleware_test.go` and no logger middleware test. Reordering the middlewares would silently strip these fields from the `grafana-data-egress` log line, and nothing would catch it. A test that checks `log.WithContextualAttributes` output for each endpoint (and that stream methods pass through) would cover this.

contracts.action: LoggerMiddleware logs via m.logger.FromContext(ctx) instead of explicit pluginId/endpoint/uname/dsName/dsUID/traceID params
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous logRequest added those fields explicitly; now ContextualLoggerMiddleware (registered just before it) puts them in ctx via log.WithContextualAttributes, and the tracing provider adds traceID
contracts.before_after: ConcreteLogger.FromContext collects args from all registered providers: the logParamsContextKey provider (log.go init) and the tracing traceID provider. Same keys as before, plus any ngalert provider attrs
contracts.visible_effect: The 'Plugin Request Completed' log line keeps the same fields. Field order changes, and alerting context attrs may appear
contracts.failure_mode: If no provider returns args, FromContext returns the base logger and the line is logged without the plugin fields. There's no error path

contracts.action: grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext type-asserts infra FromContext result to *ConcreteLogger
contracts.equivalent_path: ConcreteLogger.FromContext returns either cl or cl.New(args...), both *ConcreteLogger
contracts.before_after: The assertion always succeeds, so the d.New() fallback can't be reached
contracts.failure_mode: The fallback d.New() keeps the logger's name context and drops only the contextual attrs

contracts.action: Contextual attributes are now set in a separate ContextualLoggerMiddleware instead of inside MetricsMiddleware.instrumentPluginRequest
contracts.equivalent_path: Old instrumentPluginRequest called instrumentContext only after pluginTarget succeeded, for QueryData/CallResource/CheckHealth/CollectMetrics
contracts.before_after: Same four endpoints are instrumented and stream methods pass through as before. Attributes are now added even for unregistered plugins, but MetricsMiddleware returns ErrPluginNotRegistered before reaching it
contracts.visible_effect: Downstream loggers that call FromContext see the same attributes

summary: This refactor moves the contextual-logger attributes into a new ContextualLoggerMiddleware, placed after MetricsMiddleware and before LoggerMiddleware. LoggerMiddleware now gets its plugin, endpoint, user, datasource and trace fields through the new plog.Logger.FromContext. I checked this against the infra logger: the contextual-attribute provider and the tracing traceID provider still produce the same fields, so the log output keeps its content. The *ConcreteLogger type assertion always succeeds. I found no defects. Two test-related suggestions: the TestLogger.FromContext fake returns a fresh logger, so nothing logged through it can be asserted, and neither the new middleware nor the fields that now depend on middleware order have tests.
